# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Assistant — verify documented staff effect (staff-assistant)

## Goal
Confirm that `staff-assistant` (Assistant, management-company) is properly defined — card data, parsed typed field, description text and docs — and that it behaves exactly as documented, by adding or tightening a behavioural test that asserts its documented effect and scope. This card is one of 26 per-card verification children under the parent audit epic `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND`.

## Documented effect (authoritative: GDD Appendix D.4)

- **Ability:** +2 hand slots
- **Scope:** player hand capacity (street-wide)
- **Backing data:** handSlotsAdded=2
- **Engine consumer:** maxHandSize (WeekStart / AiStrategy)
- **Existing behavioural test file:** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Definition verified.** `staff-assistant` in `src/card-data.csv` carries the documented backing data (handSlotsAdded=2), the `description` text states the same effect at the same magnitude using the ×100 consistency rule, and `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` agree.
2. **Parsed field verified.** The typed `StaffCard` field(s) resolve to the documented value (via `parseStaffEffect` for the `effect` column, or the dedicated column) — asserted in a test.
3. **Behavioural test added or tightened.** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` (or a new focused test file) contains at least one behavioural test that asserts the documented effect AND its scope (player hand capacity (street-wide)) — not merely that the card can be hired. The test fails if the effect is absent, mis-valued or leaks outside its documented scope.
4. **Card-level verifier covers it.** `verifyStaffCard` (`tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts`) asserts the same data field, so `unitTestStatus` for `staff-assistant` cannot report `pass` vacuously.
5. **Docs updated.** Code comments and the relevant docs reflect any change made while closing this card; no documentation drift remains for this card.
6. **All tests pass.**

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-assistant` row.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard` typed fields.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — `parseStaffEffect` / template rebuild.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — effect consumer wiring.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts` — behavioural test to extend.
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/runners.ts` — `verifyStaffCard`.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — card catalog row.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — GDD Appendix D.4 authoritative design.

## Impact

Players who hire the Assistant can rely on its printed ability (+2 hand slots, scope: player) actually happening.

# Action classification for Summary tab

Add an optional `action` property to the `LogEntry` type and set it at every player- and AI-initiated action `addLog` call site. Turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows deliberately leave it unset, so the Summary tab can structurally distinguish action rows from summary rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Action classification is structural, not textual: the turn record exposes an explicit action marker (an optional category on `LogEntry`, set wherever a player- or AI-initiated action is logged), so no rendered action row depends on matching log message text.
- `LogEntry` in `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` carries an optional `action` field (a string categorising the action type).
- Every `addLog` call site that records a player- or AI-initiated action (placing a business, hiring staff, playing an upgrade/event, moving a card to hand, selling, laying off, closing a street card, loans, challenge completions) sets the `action` field to a consistent category string.
- Turn headers and per-turn monetary summary rows (income/reputation lines) carry no `action` marker.
- A guard test asserts that every known action-producing `addLog` call site sets the marker, catching regressions.
- All existing tests pass.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add optional `action` to `LogEntry`
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` and all `addLog` call sites — set the marker at action sites
- `tests/main-street/log-entry-action-marker.test.ts` — guard test

## Minimal Implementation
- Add optional `action?: string` to the `LogEntry` interface.
- Enumerate action category constants for each action type.
- Set the `action` field at each `addLog` call site that records a player- or AI-initiated action.
- Leave turn headers and monetary summary rows unset.

## Deliverables
- Updated `LogEntry` type, marked call sites, guard test.

## Dependencies
None — this is a foundational, additive change.

# Attribute one-off ledger deltas to their source for the Turn Summary tooltip

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary one-off row presents only a reconciliation formula
(`net change − income − expenses − incident`) because
`TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas` / `OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffDeltas` store a **residual**
with no per-source attribution. The player cannot see whether the one-off came
from market purchases, market sales, event plays, Community Favour exchanges,
or loan effects.

## Users

- **The human player** — wants to understand what caused a positive or negative
  one-off figure in the Turn Summary, so they can plan MarketPhase actions more
  effectively on the next day.
- **Competitive players** — want the same attribution on their own seat's one-off
  row in the competitive panel.

### User stories

- _As a player, I want the Turn Summary one-off tooltip to list each source
  (market purchase, market sale, event play, Community Favour, loan effect)
  with its signed amount, so I can see what drove the one-off figure._
- _As a competitive player, I want my own seat's one-off row to show the same
  per-source attribution as the single-player panel._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **TurnLedger gains a `oneOffBreakdown` field** — an array of `{ label: string; coins: number; reputation: number }` entries, alongside the existing residual `oneOffDeltas` (which stays for reconciliation and absent-safe fallback). The array is populated during `buildTurnLedger` and the competitive closing.
2. **OwnerRoundLedger gains `oneOffBreakdown`** — same shape as `TurnLedger.oneOffBreakdown`; optional and absent-safe (consumers render zero or the legacy formula).
3. **Attribution sources captured during the turn** — `buildTurnLedger` accepts
   additional inputs for per-source deltas: market purchase cost, market sale
   proceeds, event-play coin effect, Community Favour exchange (coins→rep and
   rep→coins), and loan effect (repayment or bailout). The residual
   `oneOffDeltas.coins` is recomputed as `netCoinChange − incomeCoins −
   ongoingTotal − incidentCoinChange` and remains the authoritative reconciling
   figure; the breakdown entries sum to the same residual (with a small tolerance
   for rounding, documented in the model).
4. **`buildOneOffLineTooltip` renders per-source attribution** — when
   `oneOffBreakdown` is present, it lists each source with its signed amount on
   its own line (e.g. `Market purchase: −120`, `Market sale: +80`). The
   reconciliation formula remains at the bottom as a checksum line. When
   `oneOffBreakdown` is absent (legacy ledgers), the tooltip falls back to the
   existing formula-only format.
5. **All new copy is localisable** — through the existing `t()` /
   `registerLocale` system with English defaults registered at module load.
6. **Deterministic automated tests** — cover every attribution source, the
   reconciliation identity, and the absent-safe fallback; added to the existing
   tooltip suites and run through the test skill.
7. **Documentation updated** — `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   ("End-of-Turn Turn Summary Ledger and Tooltips" section) documents the new
   one-off attribution; JSDoc in `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` /
   `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` reflects the new model.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

The Turn Summary one-off row now explains itself — every market purchase, sale,
event play, Community Favour exchange, and loan effect shows its individual
contribution so the player understands exactly what drove the figure.

## Constraints

- **Must stay absent-safe.** Older ledgers without `oneOffBreakdown` render the
  legacy reconciliation formula only — no regressions.
- **Deterministic.** No new RNG consumption; every figure comes from committed
  ledger data or the engine's own per-action state.
- **One sentence of copy per source** — tooltips must remain presentational;
  no layout changes.
- **Reconciliation is authoritative.** The residual `oneOffDeltas` remains the
  ground-truth figure; breakdown entries must reconcile to it.
- **Do not invent attribution.** Where the engine has no per-source data, the
  tooltip falls back to the formula.

## Existing state

- **TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas** (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): `{ coins,
  reputation }` — computed as residual
  `netCoinChange − incomeCoins − ongoingTotal − incidentCoinChange`.
- **OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffDeltas** (optional, same shape): residual per seat.
- **buildTurnLedger** (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): accepts
  `TurnLedgerInputs` (income, ongoingCosts, incident, coins, reputation, score)
  — no per-source data flows through.
- **buildOneOffLineTooltip** (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`):
  renders a single reconciliation formula string using `oneOffFormula` i18n key.
- **Competitive closing** (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`): mirrors the
  single-player residual formula per seat.
- **Market phase** (`src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`):
  modifies `state.resourceBank.coins` directly but does not track per-transaction
  attribution.
- **Community Favour** (`src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts`): modifies coins and
  reputation directly; no attribution tracking.
- **Event plays** (`src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`): apply coin/rep effects
  directly; event-play coin deltas are tracked in `SlotPhaseBreakdown.eventDeltas`
  but only for income-phase events, not MarketPhase event plays.
- **Loan effects** (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`):
  bank-loan repayments and bailouts modify coins during closing; no per-source
  tracking.
- **Projection model** (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`): copies
  `ledger.oneOffDeltas` into `PLProjection.oneOff`; no breakdown field.
- **Tests**: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` (612 lines,
  tooltip unit tests); `tests/main-street/turn-summary-model.test.ts` (ledger
  model tests).

## Desired change

1. **Extend `TurnLedger` and `OwnerRoundLedger`** with an optional
   `oneOffBreakdown: { label: string; coins: number; reputation: number }[]`
   field.
2. **Extend `TurnLedgerInputs`** with per-source delta fields:
   `marketPurchaseCost`, `marketSaleProceeds`, `eventPlayCoinEffect`,
   `communityFavourDelta` (signed), `loanEffect`. These are passed through from
   the closing entry points.
3. **Capture attribution in MarketPhase and loan paths** — add per-transaction
   tracking in `placeBusinessFromMarket`, `sellCard`, `resolveEvent`,
   `exchangeCommunityFavour`, and the loan repayment/bailout paths so that
   closing receives the data.
4. **Populate `oneOffBreakdown` in `buildTurnLedger`** — map per-source deltas
   to labelled entries, compute the residual, and assert the reconciliation
   identity (with documented rounding tolerance).
5. **Update `buildOneOffLineTooltip`** — render the breakdown list when present,
   followed by the reconciliation formula as a checksum.
6. **Update the competitive closing** to thread per-seat attribution data
   (reusing the same per-source tracking fields on `OwnerRoundLedger`).
7. **Add i18n keys** for each attribution source label and the checksum line.
8. **Extend tests** — model-level tests for `oneOffBreakdown` population,
   tooltip tests for every source and the fallback, and reconciliation
   assertions.
9. **Update docs** — the ledger/tooltip section in
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and JSDoc in the tooltip/projection
   modules.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnLedger`, `OwnerRoundLedger`,
  `TurnLedgerInputs` with `oneOffBreakdown` and per-source delta inputs.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — thread per-source data through
  `buildTurnLedger`; populate breakdown; handle deferred-closing and
  `finishDeferredEndOfTurn` paths.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — thread per-seat attribution into
  `OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffBreakdown`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend `PLProjection.oneOff` with
  breakdown data; pass through to tooltip builder.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — `buildOneOffLineTooltip`
  render logic, new i18n keys.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — Community Favour attribution capture.
- `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` — market purchase attribution.
- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — market sale attribution.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — event-play attribution for MarketPhase.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — loan
  effect attribution.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-model.test.ts` — model-level breakdown tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — per-source tooltip tests.

## Related work

- `MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9` — *Full breakdown in tooltips of end of turn dialog*
  (parent; this item was deferred from this work item's A3 as a follow-up).
- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — *Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger* (parent: attached
  the tooltips this item deepens).
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — *Bank Loans epic* (loan repayment/bailout attribution
  is part of this item's scope).
- `MS-0MWBZDVCH008P8X5` — *Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn
  Summary seats* (sibling deferred item; no overlap — this item adds attribution
  to the one-off row for all seats).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — Attribution granularity.** Sources are: market purchase (cost), market
  sale (proceeds), event play (coin effect), Community Favour (coins→rep or
  rep→coins, shown as a single entry with signed coin delta), and loan effects
  (repayment or bailout). If the producer wants card-level detail (which card
  name), that is a follow-up. **Recommended:** source-level labels are sufficient
  for the tooltip; card-level detail is tracked as a follow-up.
- **A2 — Rounding tolerance.** Floating-point arithmetic across multiple sources
  may produce a 1-coin rounding drift from the residual. The breakdown entries
  absorb the drift on the last entry. **Recommended:** document the tolerance in
  the model; reconcile to the residual, not to zero.
- **A3 — Competitive parity.** Competitive seats use the same per-source
  attribution as single-player. `OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffBreakdown` mirrors the
  single-player structure. **Recommended:** parity across all tabs.
- **A4 — Loan effects split.** Bank-loan repayment (negative) and bailout
  (positive, if different from repayment) are separate entries. **Recommended:**
  separate entries where both exist.

**Risks**

- **Engine mutation risk:** adding per-transaction tracking means mutating state
  during MarketPhase / closing. Mitigation: use dedicated tracking fields that do
  not affect game logic; keep them serialised (checkpoint-safe) so a save/load
  round-trip preserves the data.
- **Rounding drift:** multiple signed additions may not reconcile exactly.
  Mitigation: last-entry absorption documented in the model; assert with a
  tolerance in tests.
- **Scope creep:** the producer might want card-level detail (which specific card
  was purchased/sold). Mitigation: source-level labels only for now; card-level
  detail as a follow-up.

**Headline:** The business Manage Card stops laying off whichever staff member happened to be hired last: it now lists every member employed at that business, one row each with its own `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`, and an explicit confirm step quoting the exact coins and reputation before anything is charged.

## Problem statement

The Manage Card dialog is the only door for letting business staff go, but it never asks *who*: both `[ Move staff ]` and `[ Lay off ]` act on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`). A business holding two or more members therefore exposes one control per action that silently targets the newest hire, and the lay-off executes with no cost preview and no confirmation.

## Users

- **Main Street player with a staffed business (hands-on)** — employs several specialists and wants to change the team.
  - As a player, I want to see everyone employed at this business in one place, with their effect and salary, so that I can decide which specialist is worth keeping.
  - As a player, I want to press a button that belongs to the member I mean, so that I never fire the wrong specialist by accident.
  - As a player, I want the exact coins and reputation the lay-off will charge shown before I commit, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.
- **Main Street player chasing business efficiency (economy-focused)** — compares each member's salary against its local effect.
  - As a player, I want each row's salary next to the member's effect, so that I can judge the cut by its savings.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs both lay-off doors to state one rule the same way.
  - As QA, I want the quoted cost to equal the charge that lands, so that a skill discount or a clamp cannot silently diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an **employed-staff section** with exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear. Each row shows the member's name, its role/benefit summary (from a shared formatter, not a UI-invented string) and its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.

Because the per-row labels are short, the section states both costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`) so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip. No control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.

## Impact

A player who has hired several specialists at one business can finally pick which one leaves — seeing each member's effect, salary and the exact lay-off price first — instead of a single button that always fires the newest hire.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.** That item lands the salary-scaled reputation rule in `letGoStaffMember()` and exports `layOffReputationCost(salary)`. This item consumes that helper and the same lay-off confirm standard; the formula is not re-litigated here.

This item reuses the shared confirm content builder and cost helpers rather than writing a second quoting implementation; if that child lands the confirm local to the roster dialog, this item factors the shared content builder out and both call it.
- **No engine change.** No new command and no new persisted state. Membership is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each action; lay-off stays `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable) and relocation stays `moveStaffCommand` (1 action).
- **Address by id, never by index.** `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` is index-based, so a click resolves the row's member id to a current index at click time and refuses when the member is gone.
- **Pure model first.** Row building, salary/cost resolution and confirm copy live in a Phaser-free module so they are unit-testable; the overlay only draws.
- **One source of truth for figures.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off reputation cost from `layOffReputationCost`; the move destinations and 1-action cost from `buildMoveStaffAffordance`. No UI- or model-local arithmetic.

**Goal:** As a player about to let someone go, I want a confirm step that quotes the exact coin and reputation cost, so that I never fire a member without seeing the price first.

Part of **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (Company roster overlay).

## Context

- Appendix Q2 (`wl show MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA`) decided: per-row `[ Lay off ]` **plus** a confirm dialog quoting the cost, because firing costs real coins and reputation.
- Mirror the existing buy-and-place premium confirm dialog's structure in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` rather than inventing a new pattern.
- The lay-off must stay undoable and must go through the existing command: `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps `letGoStaffMember()` in a snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each roster row offers `[ Lay off ]`; activating it opens a confirm step quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (the figure actually charged, clamped at 0) and the reputation cost, both read from the roster model's row for that member — never recomputed in the overlay.
- `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand(state, member.staffIndex)` through the scene's undo manager, and `[ Cancel ]` dismisses the confirm step with no state change (asserted: coins, reputation and `state.staffCards` are unchanged).
- After a confirmed lay-off the roster refreshes in place without being reopened: the fired row disappears, the footer count and total salary change, and the Staff Pile's stack/count reflect the removal; when the last member leaves the roster shows the empty state text.
- A confirmed lay-off remains undoable: after undo, the member is back in `state.staffCards`, coins and reputation are restored, and the roster shows the restored row.
- Browser/render tests in `tests/main-street/company-roster.browser.test.ts` cover the confirm text quoting model figures, `[ Cancel ]` no-op, `[ Confirm ]` lay-off with post-change row/footer assertions, the empty state after the final lay-off, and the undo restore.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `[ Lay off ]` per row and an in-panel confirm state (or a small confirm dialog) quoting name / coins / reputation.
- Wire `[ Confirm ]` to `letGoStaffCommand()` via the scene's undo manager, then rebuild the roster rows from `buildCompanyRoster()` in place.
- Extend the render tests for confirm, cancel, refresh, empty state and undo.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — per-row `[ Lay off ]`, confirm step, in-place rebuild.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand()` (reference; unchanged).
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — quoted costs (reference).
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.browser.test.ts` — confirm/cancel/refresh/undo tests.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the roster overlay item (the confirm step lives in that dialog).

## Deliverables

Confirm step, command wiring, undo coverage, render tests.

## Impact

A player can let go any management-company staff member straight from the roster after seeing the exact coin and reputation cost up front, and can undo the decision if they change their mind.

**Goal:** As QA, I want the business-staff row model's contract pinned by tests before it is implemented, so that the Manage Card's rows, salaries and lay-off quote cannot drift from what the engine actually charges.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- Today the Manage Card dialog filters its member list inline and always acts on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`), so nothing in the codebase pins "this row belongs to this member".
- The model under test does not exist yet — the sibling model item introduces `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)`, `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)` and `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` in a Phaser-free module.
- `layOffReputationCost(salary)` is landed by **MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18** (engine: salary-scaled lay-off reputation cost); the salary resolves through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- The engine effect the quote must match: `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) removes the member, deducts one turn's effective salary clamped at 0 and the reputation cost, and deregisters it from the business's `employedStaff`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests in `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` cover the pure model — membership filtering for the slot, ordering, per-row salary, coin clamp, the reputation quote per row, id-addressing and staleness, and the empty case — and land **before** the model is implemented (the suite fails for the right reason: the module or its exports are absent).
- A test pins the confirm step's quoted cost to the effect of `letGoStaffMember()` (quoted == charged), including a discounted-salary member whose effective salary differs from its raw `ongoingCost`: the coins and reputation actually deducted equal the row's `layOffCoins` / `layOffReputation` and the figures in `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)`.
- The membership test proves management-company staff never appear in a business's rows (a slotless `state.staffCards` member), and that a member employed at a different slot is excluded.
- The staleness test proves a row whose member id is no longer present in `state.staffCards` resolves to "gone" (no index is handed to `letGoStaffCommand`) instead of silently addressing a shifted index.
- The empty case asserts `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)` is true and `buildBusinessStaffRows` returns `[]` when nobody is employed at the slot, and false/non-empty otherwise.

## Minimal implementation

- Write the test file with hand-built `MainStreetState` fixtures (street grid business at a level whose capacity the case needs, `staffCards` with and without `employedAtSlot`), reusing the fixture style of `tests/main-street/staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`.
- Import the not-yet-existing model module so the red state is explicit; do not stub the model inside the test file.
- Keep the quoted == charged test engine-first: run `letGoStaffMember()` on a cloned state and compare deltas with the model's quote.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` — **new**: the model specification tests above.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — **new (sibling model item)**: the module under test; this item only imports it.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffMember()`, `getEmploymentCapacity()` (reference).
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryCost()`, `getSalaryScopeSkills()`, `isBusinessStaffCard()` (reference).

## Dependencies

- **MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18** (engine: salary-scaled lay-off reputation cost) — `layOffReputationCost()` must exist for the quoted == charged pin.
- Blocks the model item: the tests are the definition of done for it.

## Deliverables

Failing-first unit test file covering rows, ordering, salary, clamp, reputation quote, id-addressing/staleness, the empty case and quoted == charged.

data.description:
**Goal:** As a Main Street player with a staffed business, I want each employed member's row — its role, its benefit and its real per-turn salary, with the exact cost of letting it go — computed once in a testable module, so that what the Manage Card shows is the engine's own arithmetic and never a UI-invented figure.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- The dialog currently builds its member list inline (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:700-704`) and shows only a joined name line — no salary, no per-member cost.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders `• <name> (<types>) — <description>` lines for the street tooltip; the roster model item (**MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM**) factors the per-member role line out of it. This item consumes that shared formatter rather than re-inventing the text.
- `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) already accepts an explicit member id and resolves legal destinations through `canMoveStaffOnBusiness`.
- Employment capacity is `getEmploymentCapacity(state, slot)` = `max(1, level + 1)` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:923`); the largest shipped business `maxLevel` is 2, so the largest capacity in play today is **3**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new pure module — no Phaser imports — exposes `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)`, `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)` and `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)`; each row carries `{ memberId, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation, moveEnabled, moveDestinations }`.
- `buildBusinessStaffRows` returns exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear — ordered deterministically in hire order (oldest first, i.e. `state.staffCards` order).
- Each row's role/benefit summary comes from the shared `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` (factored out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary()`, not a UI-invented string) and its salary is its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- The row's lay-off figures come from the shared helpers only: `layOffCoins` is that salary clamped at 0 and `layOffReputation` is `layOffReputationCost(salary)` from **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA**/**MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18** — the formula decided there and **not re-derived** in this module.
- `moveEnabled` and `moveDestinations` are read from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` (1-action cost, legal destination businesses), so the row never re-derives mobility.
- `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` returns the confirm step's title and body lines quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and its reputation cost, read from the row itself — the copy and arithmetic are therefore shared with the Company Roster's confirm step rather than duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

- Factor `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` so the tooltip, the roster and the Manage Card share one role/benefit text; keep the tooltip's output byte-identical.
- Implement the row builder, the empty predicate and the confirm content builder in the new module, importing `layOffReputationCost`, `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSalaryScopeSkills` and `buildMoveStaffAffordance`.
- Add `buildLayOffConfirmContent()` beside the lay-off cost helpers so both lay-off doors (business staff and the Company Roster) can call one implementation.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — **new** pure model: slot membership, hire-order rows, salary/role text, coin clamp, reputation quote, id-addressing, confirm content.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — factor `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary()`.
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — `layOffReputationCost()` (created by MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM / MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18); add the shared confirm content builder here if the roster module's cost helpers live there, otherwise keep it in the new module and import it.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryCost()`, `getSalaryScopeSkills()` (reference).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildMoveStaffAffordance()` (reference; Phaser-free builder, no change).
- `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` — the specification tests written by the test item; this item turns them green.

## Dependencies

- The test item (sibling child) — its failing suite is this item's definition of done.
- **MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM** (roster model: shared row/role formatter) — supplies the shared `formatStaffRoleLine`.
- **MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18** (engine: `layOffReputationCost()`) — supplies the reputation formula this row quotes.

## Deliverables

Phaser-free business-staff row model, shared role-line formatter, shared lay-off confirm content builder, all spec tests green.

**Goal:** As a Main Street player with several specialists employed at one business, I want every member listed as its own row with its own `[ Move ]`, so that I can see the team, compare each salary against its effect, and relocate the member I actually mean.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- `showSellConfirmation()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:690-975`) is a fixed 480×410 panel (480×360 when nobody is employed): card info, sale value, close-cost line, `[ Sell ]`/`[ Close ]`/`[ Cancel ]` at `panelY + 265`, then a single `Employed here: <names>` line at `+305` and one `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` at `+352, centerX − 110`.
- The move handler targets `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` today (`:926`), i.e. the newest hire, whatever the player clicked.
- The engine and controller already accept a member id: `s.beginStaffMove(memberId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts:1088`) → `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`), which drives `moveStaffCommand` (exactly 1 action). The affordance builder `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) resolves that member's legal destinations — no engine change is needed.
- Overlay precedent for a row list: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`:1655`); the overlay kit is `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, depths 199/200/201, all objects tracked in `s.overlayObjects` and parented into `s.hudContainer`, suppressed in `replayMode`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an employed-staff section of exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear — each row showing the member's name, its role/benefit summary from the shared formatter and its effective per-turn salary, with its own `[ Move ]`.
- Rows are ordered deterministically in hire order (oldest first) and the panel sizes itself from the row count: with no member employed the section renders nothing at all (today's empty-state behaviour); with two members employed two rows and two `[ Move ]` controls render; at a business's maximum employment capacity (`level + 1`, 3 today) every row, every button and the sell/close/cancel row are fully visible with no clipping or overlap.
- `[ Move ]` hands that row's member id to `beginStaffMove`, keeping the existing `moving-staff` choreography and the 1-action cost, and the per-member destination list from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` in its hover tooltip; no control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.
- The section states both affordance costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`), so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip.
- Browser/render tests in `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` cover: no staff section when nobody is employed; two employed members producing two rows with two `[ Move ]` controls; the *first* row's `[ Move ]` targeting the *first* member; the capacity layout with no overlap; and `[ Sell ]`, `[ Close ]` and `[ Cancel ]` still working with the rows present.

## Minimal implementation

- Replace the `Employed here: …` line and the single `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` button with a cost line plus one row per `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)` entry, laid out from a row height constant.
- Derive `panelH` from the row count (plus the fixed sell/close/cancel block) instead of the current 360/410 pair; keep every element parented and tracked exactly as today.
- Per row, create `[ Move ]` and bind its `pointerover`/`pointerout` to `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, row.memberId).tooltip` and its `pointerdown` to `dismissOverlay(...)` + `s.beginStaffMove(row.memberId)`.
- Keep the row section's teardown/rebuild in one helper so the lay-off item can re-render in place from the same code path.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showSellConfirmation()`: staff row list, per-row `[ Move ]`, cost line, panel height from row count.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — `buildBusinessStaffRows()` / `businessStaffIsEmpty()` (sibling model item).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `beginStaffMove(memberId)` (reference; unchanged signature).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (reference; already per-member).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId)` (reference) plus any new tooltip/row strings under the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` pattern.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rows, per-row move targeting, empty section, capacity layout, sell/close/cancel intact.

## Dependencies

- The model item (sibling child) — supplies `buildBusinessStaffRows()` and the shared role line.
- **MS-0MUOSULQ700186PP** (completed) — supplied `buildMoveStaffAffordance` / `[ Move staff ]`; this item only changes the target selection.

## Deliverables

Row-per-member staff section with per-row `[ Move ]`, hire-order layout, row-count-driven panel height, capacity-safe rendering, render tests.

data.description:
**Goal:** As a Main Street player about to fire a specialist, I want to press the `[ Lay off ]` that belongs to the member I mean and see the exact coins and reputation first, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- The lay-off handler currently targets the newest hire (`const target = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:944`), executes immediately, dismisses the dialog and logs the literal `Laid off <name> (−1 salary, −1 reputation)`.
- `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) in a snapshot, so the lay-off is undoable: coins, reputation and the member all come back. The reputation rule itself belongs to **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (`layOffReputationCost(salary)`) and is only quoted here.
- Confirm-overlay precedents: `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog()` (`:1227`) and `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog()` (`:994`); instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), suppressed in `replayMode`.
- The Company Roster's own confirm step is **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ**; this item must not ship a second quoting implementation — the shared `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` from the model item is the single source and, if that child rendered its confirm copy locally, this slice swaps it onto the shared builder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each row's `[ Lay off ]` opens the confirm step for that member only, quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and the reputation cost from the shared `layOffReputationCost(salary)` — the single formula decided in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA and **not re-derived here**.
- `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand` through the scene's undo manager, so the lay-off stays undoable (after undo the member, coins and reputation are restored), and `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing (coins, reputation and `state.staffCards` unchanged) and returns to the member list.
- After a confirmed lay-off the dialog stays open and re-renders in place: the row disappears and the panel shrinks to fit, and once the last member leaves the staff section disappears while `[ Sell ]`, `[ Close ]` and `[ Cancel ]` keep working.
- Rows are addressed by **member id** and resolved against `state.staffCards` at click time, so a stale row (the member is already gone, e.g. after an undo) re-renders and flashes feedback instead of acting on a shifted index.
- The activity-log entry and confirmation flash quote the charges actually applied — e.g. `Laid off <name> (−<coins> coins, −<reputation> reputation)` — replacing the hard-coded `−1 salary, −1 reputation` strings.
- Browser/render tests cover two employed members producing two rows with two `[ Lay off ]` controls, the *first* row's `[ Lay off ]` laying off the *first* member (the regression this item exists for), confirm and cancel behaviour, the in-place refresh after a lay-off, and the section disappearing when the last member leaves; the existing one-member lay-off test is updated to go through the confirm step.

## Minimal implementation

- Bind each row's `[ Lay off ]` to open the confirm overlay built from `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)`, keeping the row list beneath it.
- On `[ Confirm ]`: re-resolve the row's member id to a current `state.staffCards` index; refuse with feedback when the member is gone; otherwise execute `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` through `s.undoManager`, log/flash the applied figures, then rebuild the row section in place and `s.refreshAll()` + `s.refreshUndoRedoButtons(...)`.
- On `[ Cancel ]`: dismiss only the confirm layer and return to the rows untouched.
- Point the Company Roster's confirm step at the same `buildLayOffConfirmContent()` if it duplicated the copy.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — per-row `[ Lay off ]`, confirm overlay, id→index resolution, in-place rebuild, panel resize.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` and the row's `layOffCoins` / `layOffReputation` (model item).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand()` (reference; unchanged).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffMember()` / `layOffReputationCost()` (reference; formula owned by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRoster.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — the Company Roster's confirm step (MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ) if it needs re-pointing at the shared builder.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — multi-member lay-off targeting, confirm/cancel, refresh, empty section.

## Dependencies

- The rows/`[ Move ]` slice (sibling child) — supplies the row section and its rebuild helper.
- **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (parent blocker) — the salary-scaled `layOffReputationCost()` and the lay-off confirm standard this step follows.
- **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ** (Company Roster confirm step) — the other door sharing the same confirm content; this item unifies the copy with it.

## Deliverables

Per-row `[ Lay off ]` with a quoted confirm step, undoable execution, in-place refresh, stale-row safety, applied-charge log and flash, render tests.

data.title: Verification: full suite and end-to-end flow

data.description:
## Problem

`.pi/test-config.json` declares named test `groups`, and `run_tests.py`'s changed-scope selection is **group-first**: `changed_scope_selection()` returns the winning group's commands and never also runs the changed files' own tests (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `select_group_from_changed_files`). Two consequences surfaced while implementing `MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2` (Staff Pile):

1. **Changed test files can be skipped.** A slice that edits `src/layouts/*.json` + `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` wins the `hand-bottom-anchor-browser` group, whose command runs only `tests/main-street/hand-bottom-anchor.browser.test.ts` — so the *changed* `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` never ran in changed scope. A knowingly-wrong assertion in the new anchor test passed the finish gate and was only caught by the dev-push full suite.
2. **No group covers several frequently-touched modules.** Nothing matches `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`, `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, so their tests are only selected by convention mapping — and any group that matches one *other* changed file (e.g. `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`) takes precedence and replaces that selection (a renderer slice ran `webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` and nothing else).

## Desired change
